# Geometry and Surface Priors

Also called: Surface Priors, Geometric Constraints, SDF-Gaussian Consistency

## Overview
Geometry and Surface Priors address the inherent lack of explicit surface structure in [vanilla 3D Gaussian Splatting](#2257-3d-gaussian-splatting-3dgs-preliminaries.md) (3DGS), which produces "floating" ellipsoids rather than coherent, watertight meshes [S1]. These methods enforce geometric consistency by integrating external priors—such as neural Signed Distance Functions (SDFs), monocular depth estimates, or normal maps—into the [training loop](#4290-training-loop.md), ensuring that Gaussian primitives align with the underlying physical surface [S1]. Unlike siblings that rely on post-hoc mesh extraction or opacity level-sets, these approaches embed surface constraints directly into the optimization objective [S1].

## Shared principles
All methods in this family share the goal of aligning the discrete 3D [Gaussian representation](#5918-gaussian-based-representation.md) with a continuous or metric surface definition. The core mechanism involves adding [geometric loss](#7475-geometric-baseline-regularization.md) terms to the standard photometric rendering loss. Common strategies include:
1.  **[SDF](#1466-signed-distance-fields-sdf.md) Consistency:** Encouraging the signed distance values of Gaussian centers to be zero, aligning them with an implicit surface [S1].
2.  **Normal Consistency:** Minimizing the angular difference between normals derived from the Gaussians (or rendered normals) and normals predicted by a prior network (e.g., SDF gradient or depth estimator) [S1].
3.  **Depth Alignment:** Ensuring the closest Gaussian to a pixel aligns with rendered or estimated depth values [S1].

## Subtopics

### NeuSG
[NeuSG](#9172-neusg.md) integrates the NeRF-based surface reconstruction technique NeuS into the 3DGS representation to transfer explicit surface properties to the Gaussian primitives [S1]. It solves the problem of vanilla 3DGS producing "floating" ellipsoids by enforcing geometric consistency between the Gaussians and a learned Signed Distance Function (SDF) [S1][S2, unofficial]. Unlike siblings that rely on post-hoc mesh extraction or opacity level-sets, NeuSG integrates surface priors directly into the training loop [S1].

### GSDF
[GSDF](#9205-gsdf.md) encourages consistency between a neural Signed Distance Function (SDF) and [3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS)](#1174-3d-gaussian-splatting-3dgs.md) to enhance geometry reconstruction quality [S1]. It leverages neural SDFs for surface reconstruction to recover more detailed mesh structures, a strategy inspired by NeRF-based methods [S2, unofficial]. It differs from siblings like NeuSG by explicitly transferring surface properties to the 3DGS representation, and from Surface and Geometry Alignment by focusing on the zero-level set consistency of Gaussians themselves.

### GaussianPro
#### definition
- [S1] A method that considers neighboring views' normal direction consistency to produce better reconstruction results.
#### step
- [S1] Introduces a progressive propagation strategy for updating Gaussians, considering normal consistency between neighboring views.
- [S1] Adds plane constraints to guide the growth of 3D [Gaussian Splatting](#946-gaussian-splatting.md).

### Monocular Depth Scale Alignment
#### definition
- [S2, unofficial] A post-optimization step to resolve the up-to-scale problem in 3D scenes reconstructed from multi-view images by aligning the scale of optimized 3D Gaussians with metric-scale monocular depth estimates.
#### pitfall
- [S2, unofficial] Unlike [original 3DGS](#2805-3d-gaussian-splatting-rendering-software.md), this method avoids pruning initial COLMAP points to prevent affecting the distribution of optimized Gaussian parameters, ensuring fair comparison with other studies.

### Sparse-view 3D Gaussian Splatting with Depth Priors
#### definition
- [S1] Methods targeting 3D reconstruction from sparse-view inputs by introducing depth inputs estimated by a pre-trained 2D network.
#### step
- [S1] It further removes Gaussians with incorrect depth values and utilizes the [text cuts off].

### 3DGSR
#### definition
- [S1] A method that encourages consistency between Signed Distance Function (SDF) and 3DGS to enhance geometry reconstruction quality.

### DN-Splatter
#### definition
- [S1] A method that utilizes depth and normal priors captured from common devices or predicted from general-purpose networks to enhance the reconstruction quality of 3DGS.

## Background
The discrete nature of 3D Gaussian Splatting often results in geometry that is difficult to extract as a clean mesh, leading to "popping" artifacts and floating structures [S1]. Early attempts to mitigate this included [tile-based sorting](#12180-sorting-and-rendering-pipeline-optimization.md) (StopThePop) [S1]. Subsequent work introduced explicit geometric constraints: GaussianPro used normal consistency and plane constraints [S1]; NeuSG and GSDF incorporated neural SDFs to enforce zero-level set alignment [S1]; and sparse-view methods leveraged pre-trained 2D depth estimators to supervise geometry [S1]. More recently, scale alignment techniques have addressed the metric scale ambiguity inherent in image-only reconstruction pipelines [S2, unofficial].
